stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Many visitors assume that a dead tree left standing in a forest is ______ to the animals that live around it. Ecologist Rosa Delgado's survey of one oak woodland challenges that assumption: she found woodpeckers, bats, beetles, and owls nesting in the standing dead trees, more of them than in any of the living ones.
explanation: Start with what the evidence shows: many animals depend on dead trees, so the trees are valuable. Then look at the reversal. The survey 'challenges that assumption,' so the assumption in the blank must be the opposite of what the survey found. The opposite of valuable is 'useless.' Read it back with the negative included: visitors assume dead trees are useless, and the survey shows they are not. This is the exact move behind the hidden-negative questions on the test: when a word like 'challenges' sits between the blank and the evidence, the blank is the reverse of the evidence.

A.why: You matched the blank to the evidence and skipped the reversal. The survey shows that dead trees are essential, but the blank holds the assumption the survey challenges. That makes 'essential' the opposite of the answer.

B.why: Nothing in the survey says whether dead trees harm animals. Finding animals nesting in them does not challenge an assumption about harm, so this word does not set up the contrast the passage describes.

D.why: Whether animals can see the trees has nothing to do with the survey. Counting nests says nothing about visibility, so there is no assumption here for the evidence to challenge.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Some early critics dismissed the blues as little more than ______ entertainment. Recordings from the 1920s tell a different story: performers revised their songs carefully from one session to the next, refining lyrics and guitar parts the way a composer revises a score.
explanation: The evidence shows careful, deliberate craft. The critics' view is 'little more than ______,' and the recordings 'tell a different story.' Both phrases tell you the critics believed the opposite of what the evidence shows. The opposite of carefully crafted is 'throwaway.' Read it back: critics called the blues little more than throwaway entertainment, and the recordings show otherwise. 'Little more than' is one of the most common hidden negatives on the test. It belittles whatever fills the blank, so the blank has to be something dismissive.

A.why: You took the word from the evidence, which describes careful revision, and skipped the reversal. The critics were dismissing the blues, and nobody dismisses something as 'little more than polished.' This choice is the recordings' view, not the critics'.

C.why: You matched the topic, because the passage mentions recordings, instead of the function. Careful revision does not argue against the blues being recorded, so this word gives the recordings nothing to contradict.

D.why: This word fits the subject of the blues but not the logic. Evidence about careful songwriting does not challenge whether the music was rural, so it cannot be the view that the recordings overturn.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: Before the town raised its minimum wage, several economists predicted that the change would make local employers ______ to hire new workers. The opposite happened: in the following year, the town's restaurants added 120 jobs, more than in any of the previous five years.
explanation: The evidence shows that employers hired more. The words 'The opposite happened' tell you the prediction in the blank must be the reverse of that result. The reverse of hiring more is being unwilling to hire, which is 'reluctant.' Read it back: economists predicted employers would be reluctant to hire, and instead hiring rose. On the test, when a prediction, expectation, or belief is followed by 'the opposite happened,' 'instead,' or 'yet,' the blank belongs to the side that was proved wrong.

A.why: You read the hiring numbers and put them straight into the blank. Employers did turn out to be eager, but the blank is the prediction that 'the opposite' of what happened would occur, so it has to point the other way.

B.why: Nothing in the passage says that a wage law forces anyone to hire. This choice adds a legal requirement that the text never mentions, and rising job numbers are not the 'opposite' of such a requirement.

C.why: Training has nothing to do with whether hiring went up or down. This word does not set up a prediction that the job numbers could reverse.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
stimulus: For decades, archaeologists believed that the hilltop settlement at Kerevo had been ______. Excavations in 2019 overturned that belief: the team uncovered house floors rebuilt eleven times, one on top of another, over roughly three centuries of continuous use.
explanation: The evidence shows that people lived at the site for about three hundred years, so it was long-lasting. 'Overturned that belief' tells you the earlier belief said the opposite. The opposite of long-lasting is 'temporary.' Read it back: archaeologists believed the settlement was temporary, and three centuries of rebuilt floors overturned that belief. This is the 'view that gets knocked down' pattern you will see on the test. The blank sits inside the old belief, so it has to clash with the new finding.

B.why: You matched the blank to the excavation, which does show a permanent settlement, and skipped 'overturned.' The blank is the belief that the evidence knocked down, so it must be the opposite of 'permanent.'

C.why: The excavation found rebuilt house floors, not walls or defenses. Evidence about how long people stayed does not overturn a belief about fortification, so this word does not fit the reversal.

D.why: Rebuilt floors over three centuries tell you how long the site was used, not how rich its people were. This word gives the excavation nothing to overturn.
